To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

fs-laser writing of waveguides in phosphate glasses enables to produce high-performance passive waveguide amplifiers (with 2.5 dB/m gain and 1.5 dB/m propagation loss at 1550 nm) and waveguide lasers (with slope efficiencies of up to 42%) with a single fs-laser pulse train and with the same laser writing parameters, by simply changing the laser writing conditions.
we show that fs-laser induced local composition modification can also be used to produce active waveguides in glass with high optical gain and that these active waveguides are thermally stable.

fs-laser writing enables producing high-efficiency waveguide optical amplifiers and lasers in phosphate glasses through a local modification of the lanthanide concentration, which is the key to the refractive index change.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fabrication of high-efficiency waveguides and waveguide lasers in phosphate glasses by fs-laser irradiation.
the fabrication and characterization of active and passive waveguides produced in phosphate glass by means of fs-laser writing at high repetition rate.
the development of novel laser writing techniques for producing high-performance optical components.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the fs-laser induced local modification of the composition of the phosphate glass can be used to produce active waveguides in phosphate glass that are suitable for high-efficiency lasers and amplifiers.

this work demonstrates the potential for fs laser written active waveguide amplifiers in phosphate glass with high efficiency and thermal stability, paving the way towards the development of a new generation of compact integrated laser sources.

the local modification of glass composition induced by fs-laser irradiation enables the production of high-performance passive and active waveguides, with high refractive index contrast and high optical gains, respectively, in the same glass sample.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fs-laser irradiation enables to locally modify the glass composition and thus to produce waveguides with high optical performance.
fs-laser induced local modification of the refractive index of the glass is a very promising technique for the fabrication of integrated optical amplifiers and lasers in different types of glasses.
fs laser writing in glasses enables the fabrication of high-performance passive and active waveguides.
The main takeaway from our work is that

fs-laser writing in glasses is a versatile tool for producing waveguides with active and passive properties, enabling to produce waveguides with the desired optical properties by simply changing the writing parameters.

fs-laser irradiation can be used to produce active waveguides in a wide range of glass compositions and that the local concentration changes of the glass constituents can be used to characterize the waveguiding properties.
fs-laser induced local modification of the refractive index in a glass can also be used for producing active waveguiding structures in the glass, with high optical gains and high efficiency.
